text: Baby ASI hallucinations: the most interesting patterns per millisecond
description: Research and ideation track, artistic. No realism expected. Question: what are the minimal costs (weights, taps, ms per frame at high resolution, still real time) for a tiny net to render non-realistic, interesting patterns? Start from cellular automata. Keep the core: splat reprojection (gives 3D consistency) + push-pull fill as the baseline, certainty/hole as an input. Judge by eye (snapshot grids) and by cost, not by hole error alone.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: A net with far fewer than nice-net's ~5k weights still produces patterns judged interesting, at a fraction of the ms
Hand-written CA rules running on the reprojected state give 3D-consistent, lively patterns at near-zero training cost
Losses that ask for stable, rich texture instead of exact frames make nets that look more alive than nice-net
A visual overview speeds up choosing directions more than loss numbers do
Wider coarse levels carry richer large-scale structure (shapes, not just averaged colour), so hallucinations get more coherent at similar ms

status.comment: nice-net vs push-pull, free-running 120 steps (6 rollouts, 64 px): push-pull blurs (sharpness 0.98 -> 0.17 of truth, contrast 0.61 at step 96), nice-net keeps or invents structure (1.00 -> 2.14, contrast ~1.1-1.2) while its L1 is up to 40% higher: L1 rewards blur, so it cannot judge this track.
